nodes.prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 photo, the first frame of a video shot, looking like an ordinary frame from a real camera with a normal lens, not a render; true-to-life gentle colors and soft natural contrast; fine natural grain; the far background a touch softer than the foreground. No over-sharpening, no HDR, no CGI look. Image 1 is the empty half-packed kitchen: the shot takes place in exactly this room, same furniture, same light; keep the background exactly as in Image 1. Image 2 is the friend's character sheet: use it only for her face, skin tone, silver hair, round glasses, church hat and clothes. Image 3 shows the teal silicone utensils: use it only for their shape and teal color. Medium shot. The photo shows in the grandmother's kitchen cluttered with moving boxes, the friend in her moss-green dress holds a teal silicone spatula she has pulled from the white crock, looking at it. The friend: a 73-year-old Black American woman with deep brown skin, a long oval face, short close-cropped silver natural hair and large round tortoiseshell glasses worn on her face; tall and slender. She is just back from church and keeps her church hat on all afternoon: a moss-green church hat with a medium upturned brim, a matching band and a small fabric flower, worn tilted slightly to one side, her silver hair showing below it; a moss-green dress, a matching cardigan with a small brooch, a canvas tote bag on her shoulder. Every moving box is plain brown cardboard, unprinted and unlabeled, with no brand marks. Every hand has five fingers in natural proportion and a natural grip; each person has exactly two arms and two hands; nothing floats. Everyone's eyes stay off-lens; nobody looks into the camera. Look: plain daylight in a lived-in kitchen, natural color. Skin as a real camera sees it from a couple of meters away: natural, with subtle texture and slight unevenness, not retouched, not over-detailed; no airbrushed, waxy or plastic skin. Brown skin true to life: each person keeps their own skin depth and undertone, with soft natural highlights and visible detail in the shadows; palms lighter than the backs of the hands; never grey, ashy or lightened. Final check: the friend is the same woman as in her character sheet, with the same skin tone, silver hair, round glasses and moss-green church hat; nobody else wears a hat. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text.

Medium shot, 6 seconds, one continuous shot, no cuts. The image is the start frame; the shot begins exactly on it. Camera: standing on a tripod, locked off, no movement. Physics: real weight and balance; nothing moves on its own: whatever moves is moved by a visible hand or by the action. Object lock: every utensil, bowl, plate, glass, brochure and prop in the picture is a rigid solid object that keeps exactly the same shape, size, length, color and number of pieces from the first frame to the last; nothing bends, stretches, melts, warps, splits, merges, multiplies, morphs or turns into something else; nothing appears, disappears or swaps places. Whatever anyone holds stays in exactly the same grip, length and angle as in the start frame and never slides through or passes through their fingers. People: everyone in the start frame keeps the same face, age, skin tone, hair and clothes; nobody is added or replaced; bodies move with real weight, feet on the floor. Action: She turns her eyes from the spatula to her friend and asks. Living layer (only what is already in the frame moves, nothing is added): the people breathe and blink naturally; the daylight shifts a little across the boxes. Speech: the friend speaks with clear lip-sync in the voice of a Black American woman in her early seventies with Southern roots: a low, warm, unhurried alto with the calm authority of an elder and a dry wit; natural, not an announcer, not salesy. This is the one voice used for the friend in every clip of this video: keep exactly this voice, accent, age, pitch and pace. This time: casual but probing. Exactly these words, word for word, nothing added or repeated: "When'd you buy these?" The friend starts speaking at about 0.4 seconds and has finished the whole line by about 2.0 seconds at the latest; after the last word she keeps the same feeling in her face, lips close and stay closed, no sound. Everyone else stays silent. Face: alive the whole time, never frozen, never a fixed smile; the expression follows the words through the brows, eyes and mouth corners; understated, never theatrical. Everyone's eyes stay off-lens; nobody looks into the camera. Real-time pace, nothing slow-motion; the main action starts within the first second. Keep the look, lighting and natural skin of the start frame to the last second. Audio: only the friend's voice and quiet room tone of a quiet daytime kitchen; no music. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text.
